arxiv-2108-11145.title: Dynamic DV-QKD Networking in Trusted-node-free Software-Defined Optical Networks
arxiv-2108-11145.creator: Obada Alia, Rodrigo Stange Tessinari, Emilio Hugues-Salas, George T Kanellos, Reza Nejabati, Dimitra Simeonidou
arxiv-2108-11145.description: Abstract We demonstrate for the first time a four-node trusted-node-free metro network configuration with dynamic discrete-variable quantum key distribution DV-QKD networking capabilities across four optical network nodes. The network allows the dynamic deployment of any QKD link between two nodes of the network, while a QKD-aware centralised software-defined networking (SDN) controller is utilised to provide dynamicity in switching and rerouting.

arxiv-2309-13247.title: Multi-modal Domain Adaptation for REG via Relation Transfer
arxiv-2309-13247.creator: Yifan Ding Liqiang Wang, Boqing Gong
arxiv-2309-13247.description: Abstract Domain adaptation, which aims to transfer knowledge between domains, has been well studied in many areas such as image classification and object detection. However, for multi-modal tasks, conventional approaches rely on large-scale pre-training. But due to the difficulty of acquiring multi-modal data, large-scale pre-training is often impractical.

arxiv-2404-08177.title: Stoner ferromagnetism in low-angle twisted bilayer graphene at three-quarters filling
arxiv-2404-08177.creator: Kevin J. U. Vidarte, Felipe Pérez Riffo, Eric Suárez Morell, Caio Lewenkopf
arxiv-2404-08177.description: Abstract We present a theoretical investigation of the magnetic properties exhibited by twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) systems with small twist angles, where the appearance of flat minibands strongly enhances electron-electron interaction effects. We show that, at three-quarters filling of the conduction miniband, the Stoner mechanism induces a ferromagnetic polarization in the AA-stacking regions, which aligns with recent experimental observations.

britannica-1911-crevasse.title: Crevasse (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-crevasse.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-crevasse.description: Article 'Crevasse' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 7), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Switzerland, and thence universally in high mountain regions, it designates a fissure in a glacier caused by gigantic cracks in the ice-mass, sometimes of great depth, into which climbers frequently fall through a light bridge of snow which conceals the crevasse.

plos-pone-0002900.creator: Philip J. Monahan, Kevin de Souza, William J. Idsardi
plos-pone-0002900.description: PLOS ONE research article. Understanding the time course of how listeners reconstruct a missing fundamental component in an auditory stimulus remains elusive. We report MEG evidence that the missing fundamental component of a complex auditory stimulus is recovered in auditory cortex within 100 ms post stim

pmc-11431217.title: Validity of an ICD-10 Coding Algorithm for Acute Heat Illness in the Emergency Department: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-11431217.creator: Hasan Baassiri, Timothy Varghese, Kristin K. Clemens, Alexandra M. Ouédraogo, Kristine Van Aarsen, Branka Vujčić, Justin W. Yan
pmc-11431217.description: Acute heat illness (AHI) from extreme environmental heat exposure can lead to emergency department (ED) visits, hospitalization, and even death. While the ICD ninth revision codes for AHI have been validated in the U.S., there have been no studies on the validity of ICD-10 codes for AHI in Canada.

pmc-11560898.title: Neuronal basis of high frequency fMRI fluctuation: direct evidence from simultaneous recording
pmc-11560898.creator: Yang Qiao, Hanbing Lu, Yihong Yang, Yufeng Zang
pmc-11560898.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (RS-fMRI) has been extensively utilized for noninvasive investigation of human brain activity. While studies employing simultaneous recordings of fMRI and electrophysiology have established a connection between the low-frequency fluctuation (< 0.1 Hz) observed in RS-fMRI and the local field potential (LFP), it remains unclear whether the RS-fMRI signal exhibits frequency-dependent modulation, which is a well-documented phenomenon in LFP.

pmc-11651994.title: Reproducibility of proton density fat fraction assessment of thigh muscle in a multi-site, multi-vendor cohort study at 10 years after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
pmc-11651994.creator: Brendan L. Eck, Sibaji Gaj, Richard Lartey, Mei Li, Jeehun Kim, Carl S. Winalski, William Zaylor, Dongxing Xie, Ria Tilve, Kevin D. Harkins, Bruce M. Damon, Laura J. Huston, Faysal Altahawi, Nancy A. Obuchowski, Xiaodong Zhong, Kecheng Liu, Harry Friel, Dimitrios C. Karampinos, Michael V. Knopp, Mor
pmc-11651994.description: BackgroundDixon-based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) intramuscular proton density fat fraction (PDFF) is a potentially useful imaging biomarker of muscle quality. However, multi-vendor, multi-site reproducibility of intramuscular PDFF quantification, required for large clinical studies, can be strongly dependent on acquisition and processing.

pmc-12331206.title: Non-pathological facial asymmetry in adult women: an approach to bite force, occlusal contact distribution and masticatory muscle thickness
pmc-12331206.creator: Anna L Alves Fernandes, Lilian Mendes Andrade, Laís Valencise Magri, Jardel F Mazzi-Chaves, Sergio Rodrigues, Isabela Hallak Regalo, Paulo B de Vasconcelos, Selma Siéssere, Simone C Hallak Regalo, Marcelo Palinkas
pmc-12331206.description: Facial asymmetries, often subtle, can indicate imbalances that go beyond aesthetic concerns.Aim:This cross-sectional study analyzed molar bite force, occlusal contact distribution, and masseter and temporal muscle thickness in adult women with facial symmetry and slight non-pathological facial asymmetry, which generally goes unnoticed and is often considered a variation of normality.

pmc-13017813.title: Association between neonatal birthweight and maternal vaginal wall prolapse: a retrospective analysis of postpartum women
pmc-13017813.creator: Zhuwei Gao, Yuan Wang, Lichi Zhang, Hongxian Li, Aiju Chen, Yue Yuan, Xinghui Chen
pmc-13017813.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the association between neonatal birthweight (BW) and the maternal risk of anterior and posterior vaginal wall prolapse in the postpartum period.MethodsThis retrospective cross-sectional study included 864 postpartum women undergoing routine follow-ups after delivery. Participants were categorized into quartiles according to BW.

pmc-13120250.title: Advances in Targeted Toxin Therapy for Malignant Gliomas: A Narrative Review
pmc-13120250.creator: Hanish Polavarapu, Walter A. Hall
pmc-13120250.description: Malignant gliomas remain highly treatment-resistant brain tumors despite surgery and adjuvant therapies. Targeted toxin therapies represent a unique strategy that exploits receptor-mediated cellular internalization to deliver cytotoxic components that result in the irreversible inhibition of protein synthesis independent of DNA damage or cell-cycle status.

pmc-13151207.title: Microscopy underestimates submicroscopic malaria infections in Ethiopia’s southern rift valley: a community-based cross-sectional study
pmc-13151207.creator: Betelihem Jima, Biniam Wondale, Nigatu Eligo, Feven Wudineh, Teklu Wegayehu, Bernt Lindtjørn, Fekadu Massebo
pmc-13151207.description: BackgroundEfforts to control malaria face several challenges, including the presence of parasite reservoirs within the community that contribute to disease transmission. This study aimed to assess malaria prevalence among community members using microscopy and nested polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to detect parasite reservoirs in malaria-endemic settings.

pmc-13222446.title: Workplace difficulties in early-stage relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis with low physical disability
pmc-13222446.creator: Ángel Pérez-Sempere, Elena García-Arcelay, Jacobo Caruncho, Antonio Candeliere-Merlicco, Aida Orviz, Jesús Martín-Martínez, Raquel Piñar Morales, Elena Álvarez-Rodríguez, Eva M Pacheco, Laura Borrega, Ignacio Casanova, Ana B Caminero, José L Sánchez-Menoyo, Montserrat Gómez-Gutiérrez, Olga Carmona,
pmc-13222446.description: This study evaluated perceived workplace difficulties in 128 individuals with early-stage relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis and low physical disability. Significant workplace challenges were reported by 40.6% of participants. External barriers, including workplace inflexibility and professional-domestic life imbalance (median 23-item multiple sclerosis (MS) Work Difficulties Questionnaire-MSWDQ-23 score: 31.3, interquartile range 6.3–56.3), represented the highest burden.

pmc-13470205.title: Thermally-modulated dissipation dilution in 2D NEMS resonators with explicit model and temperature-stable damping
pmc-13470205.creator: Pengcheng Zhang, Luming Wang, Jiankai Zhu, Yueyang Jia, Bo Xu, Zenghui Wang, Rui Yang
pmc-13470205.description: Strain-diluted dissipation has emerged as a promising technique to modulate the quality (Q) factor of resonant nanoelectromechanical systems (NEMS). However, comprehensive understanding and precise control of this effect under varying temperatures have remained elusive. Here we investigate the temperature-modulated dissipation dilution mechanisms in two-dimensional (2D) NEMS resonators.

pmc-13485991.title: Participatory species naming as a tool for public engagement and conservation
pmc-13485991.creator: Cene Fišer, Maja Zagmajster

Linnaean binomials provide convenient identifiers for species hypotheses (Thiele and Yeates 2002, Hey 2006), linking taxonomic expertise with broader biodiversity research. If etymology can bridge biodiversity research with society at large, taxonomy has the potential to become an integral part of science communication, particularly in raising awareness about the importance of local biota.
